body:
@groundnuty Unfortunately this appears to be a consequence of evaluating the condition from the true root of the computed values from the umbrella chart. If you change `foo/requirements.yaml`'s condition to `foo1.foo-feature.enabled` you will get different results (but its not a solution). There are some other issues arising from `alias` and `conditions` not working perfectly together and there is a suggestion to change it to a relative evaluation. 

I fear breaking backwards compatibility but Id like to enable your use case here since its so efficient on disk and facilitates a flat directory structure. If you would be interested in a proposal/PR i would help support it.

It doesn't appear that aliasing is even necessary here. If a subchart's `requirements.yaml` includes `condition: foo.enabled` and I define subchart as a dependency in another chart, the only way to affect that condition is by setting `foo.enabled` _at the top level_.

This seems more like a bug in value resolution than anything. Every other value I want to override goes into `subchart.key = value`, so why would a condition in the requirements need `key = value` instead? This is especially misleading when the subchart is referring to a dependency both charts share because now my `values.yaml` looks like this:

```yaml
common-thing:
  thing1: thing2
  enabled: false
subchart:
  what: ever
```

It looks like `common-thing` is disabled, but in reality it's there purely for `subchart` to avoid having *it* require `common-thing`, thereby breaking the install with "service `my-common-thing` already exists`.

I have a similar problem. It seems like the values of the 2nd level subchart are not taken into account by helm for rendering.

/kind bug

issue.title: child chart requirements.yaml alias not respected by parent when processing values.yaml
issue.body:
I'm trying to create an umbrella chart that includes subcharts.  One of the subcharts is using `requirements.yaml` with an alias, i.e.
```
dependencies:
- name: nginx-ingress
  version: 0.22.1
  repository: https://kubernetes-charts.storage.googleapis.com
  alias: mynginx
```

The subchart is using this alias within its `values.yaml`, i.e.:
```
mynginx:
  controller:
    ingressClass: mynginx
```

This works as expected at runtime.  Running `helm template subchart.tgz --debug`: 
```
COMPUTED VALUES:
dvnginx:
  controller:
    ingressClass: dv-nginx
```

The umbrella chart build is putting the above prepackage tgz into `charts/`.  But when I run  `helm template umbrella --debug` I get:
```
COMPUTED VALUES:
umbrella:
  mynginx:
    controller:
      ingressClass: dv-nginx
  nginx-ingress:
    controller:
		...
      ingressClass: nginx
```

This breaks at runtime (the above example has more overrides that the child is making to ingress-nginx for private purposes).

The umbrella chart is not using requirements.yaml.

Is this a bug, where the aliasing is not preserved through the additional layer of nesting, or do I need to do more at umbrella level to use the child chart correctly?

Output of `helm version`:
```
Client: &version.Version{SemVer:"v2.9.0", GitCommit:"f6025bb9ee7daf9fee0026541c90a6f557a3e0bc", GitTreeState:"clean"}
Server: &version.Version{SemVer:"v2.9.0", GitCommit:"f6025bb9ee7daf9fee0026541c90a6f557a3e0bc", GitTreeState:"clean"}
```
